% Candidate only.  It is not a live-book assertion or a retirement of P21.3.
\begin{proposition}[Invariant split-toric continuous-pair independence]
\label{prop:p213-invariant-split-toric-continuous-pairs-candidate}
Let $K$ be a complete non-Archimedean field, let $\mathbb T$ be a split
$K$-torus of dimension $n$ with cocharacter lattice $N$, and put
\[
 \operatorname{trop}:\mathbb T^{\an}\longrightarrow N_{\mathbb R}.
\]
Let $O\subseteq N_{\mathbb R}$ be open and set
$V=\operatorname{trop}^{-1}(O)$.  Let $S$ be the maximal compact torus of
$\mathbb T^{\an}$, and let $T$ be a positive $\dprime$- and
$\ddprime$-closed CLD current of bidegree $(p,p)$ on $V$, where
$0\leq p\leq n-1$.  If $u,v$ are $S$-invariant continuous CLD-psh functions
on $V$ satisfying
\[
 \dprimeddprime[u]=\dprimeddprime[v],
\]
then
\[
 \dprimeddprime(uT)=\dprimeddprime(vT).
\]
Consequently, every positive closed CLD current on $V$ has the
continuous-pair Bedford--Taylor independence property for $S$-invariant
continuous psh pairs.
\end{proposition}
proof:
% Source-aware verification context for the attached P21.3 subcase only.
% This is a context dependency, not a second theorem statement.
\section*{Scope and load-bearing inputs}

The target is a restricted continuous-pair P21.3 assertion on an open inverse
image $V=\operatorname{trop}^{-1}(O)$ in a split dense torus.  It does not
make a claim for noninvariant potentials, toric boundary strata, nonsplit
tori, arbitrary toroidal charts, or the full P21.3 ambient class.

The proof uses the following precisely delimited inputs.
\begin{enumerate}
\item For the maximal compact torus $S$ and any open $O$ in the tropical
 dense stratum, BGJKK25 equation~(5.5) identifies continuous functions on
 $O$ with $S$-invariant continuous functions on
 $\operatorname{trop}^{-1}(O)$.
\item The test-form computation in the proof of BGJKK25 Proposition~5.3.10(iv)
 shows that the current of such a descended continuous function is the
 pushforward of its invariant analytic function-current.  Its ingredients are
 exactly the factorization in (5.5), continuity, and support of pulled-back
 compact top-degree forms on the canonical skeleton.  The candidate does not
 invoke the proposition's psh positivity conclusion outside its stated scope.
\item Proper pushforward commutes with $\dprime$ and $\ddprime$; this is also
 the book's \cref{prop:current-pushforward-formal}.  The tropicalization of a
 toric variety is proper, and its restriction over an open target is proper.
\item On an ordinary Euclidean ball, a zero Lagerberg $\dprimeddprime$ current
 has all distributional second partial derivatives zero, hence its continuous
 representative is affine.  The identical calculation is recorded in
 \cref{prop:ch16-cell-rigidity}.
\item An affine function of the torus moment coordinates pulls back to a
 smooth zero-Hessian CLD function (\cref{lem:ch19-toric-chart}).  Finally,
 for a positive closed current, a smooth zero-Hessian difference gives equal
 products (\cref{cor:ch16-smooth-h}).
\end{enumerate}

Please reject the candidate if any one of the following occurs: the
continuous-current pushforward calculation has a hidden psh or support
requirement; properness fails after restriction to $O$; zero tropical Hessian
does not imply the stated local affine conclusion; or the cited smooth-factor
corollary fails in the P21.3 bidegrees $0\leq p\leq n-1$.

% Candidate only.  The cited source statements and the live-book interfaces
% are listed explicitly in SOURCE_LEDGER.md.
\begin{proof}
By the invariant-function correspondence (5.5) of \cite{BGJKK25}, there
are unique finite continuous functions $\varphi,\psi$ on $O$ such that
\[
 u=\varphi\circ\operatorname{trop},\qquad
 v=\psi\circ\operatorname{trop}.
\]
The test-form computation in the proof of Proposition~5.3.10(iv) of
\cite{BGJKK25} uses only this factorization and continuity: pullbacks of
compactly supported top-degree tropical forms are supported on the canonical
skeleton.  It therefore gives, for the two present continuous functions,
\[
 [\varphi]=\operatorname{trop}_*[u],\qquad
 [\psi]=\operatorname{trop}_*[v].
\]
The same proof displays commutation of this pushforward with
$\dprimeddprime$.  Thus
\[
 \dprimeddprime[\varphi]
 =\operatorname{trop}_*\dprimeddprime[u]
 =\operatorname{trop}_*\dprimeddprime[v]
 =\dprimeddprime[\psi].
\]

Put $h=\varphi-\psi$.  On every Euclidean ball $B\Subset O$, the equality
$\dprimeddprime[h]=0$ says that every distributional second partial
derivative of $h|_B$ is zero.  Hence $h|_B$ is affine.  (Indeed each first
distributional derivative is constant on the connected ball; the continuous
function $h$ therefore equals the resulting affine function.)  Thus
$h\circ\operatorname{trop}$ is locally a smooth CLD function with zero
$\dprimeddprime$: after choosing a basis of $N$, it is locally an affine
function of the moment coordinates $-\log|\chi^m|$; in the book's notation
this is \cref{lem:ch19-toric-chart}.

Now $u-v=h\circ\operatorname{trop}$ is smooth and has zero CLD Hessian.
The closed-current Leibniz identity, equivalently
\cref{cor:ch16-smooth-h}, gives
\[
 \dprimeddprime\bigl((u-v)T\bigr)=0.
\]
Linearity of multiplication by $T$ proves the asserted equality.
\end{proof}
